tutorial.phantasia.getting_started.title: Getting Started
tutorial.phantasia.getting_started.desc: A quick overview of what Phantasia is and how to use it.
tutorial.phantasia.getting_started.s0.bo:
Phantasia is an interactive guide system installed in your modpack.

It provides 3D machine previews, step-by-step assembly walkthroughs,
and rich reference pages all without leaving the game.
tutorial.phantasia.getting_started.s1.bo:
Point at any multiblock machine in the world and hold the %s key.
A progress bar appears at the bottom of your screen if your current ui mode is HOTBAR/HOTBAR+TOOLTIP in settings.

Keep holding until it fills, the viewer opens automatically.
tutorial.phantasia.getting_started.s2.bo:
The machine name can appear in three places, whichever you prefer.

JADE: shown in the JADE HUD (top corner).
TOOLTIP: shown on the item or block tooltip.
HOTBAR: shown above your hotbar.

Change the mode in Settings. Either way, %s always works.
tutorial.phantasia.getting_started.s3.bo:
Type /phantasia to open a searchable list of every multiblock,
scene layout, and guide.

Use it any time, you don't need to be near a machine.
The Tutorials tab is also right here.
tutorial.phantasia.getting_started.s4.bo:
That's all you need to know as a player.

Open the other tabs in Tutorials for deeper dives into
guides, scripts, and scenes.
Pack authors can check the dev tutorials for more.
tutorial.phantasia.guides.title: Understanding Guides
tutorial.phantasia.guides.desc: Learn what guides are and how to read them.
tutorial.phantasia.guides.s0.title: What is a Guide?
tutorial.phantasia.guides.s0.body:
A guide is a text-and-item reference document, like a recipe card
or lore page. It can have multiple pages you scroll through.

Find guides in /phantasia under the Guides tab.
tutorial.phantasia.guides.s1.title: Reading a Guide
tutorial.phantasia.guides.s1.body:
Each page has an optional headline, body text, and an item grid.

The item grid shows ingredients, outputs, or catalysts.
Use the navigation buttons at the bottom to flip pages.
tutorial.phantasia.guides.s2.title: Pages and Navigation
tutorial.phantasia.guides.s2.body:
Use the Next/Prev buttons at the bottom of the guide or press
the arrow keys to navigate between pages.

Press ESC to close and return to the selection screen.
tutorial.phantasia.guides.s3.title: Cross-Links
tutorial.phantasia.guides.s3.body:
Guide pages can link to other guides, to scene layouts, or to
machine scripts. Clicking a link opens that content directly.

This lets pack authors build a flowing documentation flow
from overview to details to assembly.
tutorial.phantasia.scripts.title: Understanding Scripts
tutorial.phantasia.scripts.desc: Learn how step-by-step machine walkthroughs work.
tutorial.phantasia.scripts.s0.title: What is a Script?
tutorial.phantasia.scripts.s0.body:
A script is a step-by-step 3D walkthrough for a single multiblock.

It loads the machine into a virtual world preview, then walks you
through each layer with camera movements and instructions.

Open one from /phantasia under Multiblocks.
tutorial.phantasia.scripts.s1.title: Following the Steps
tutorial.phantasia.scripts.s1.body:
Each step focuses the camera on a specific part of the machine.

The caption strip above the timeline shows the current instruction.
Use the scrubber or play/pause to move through the walkthrough.
The 3D preview updates to show only the relevant blocks.
tutorial.phantasia.scripts.s2.title: Variants
tutorial.phantasia.scripts.s2.body:
The right panel holds machine-specific options.

Click to expand it, you'll find Show/Layer/Build controls
and extra tools. Your layer and build-order state persists.
tutorial.phantasia.scenes.title: Understanding Scenes
tutorial.phantasia.scenes.desc: Learn how multi-machine scene layouts work.
tutorial.phantasia.scenes.s0.title: What is a Scene?
tutorial.phantasia.scenes.s0.body:
A scene places multiple machines together at offsets from a
shared origin, like a factory floor layout.

Each machine is controlled independently but shown together
in the same 3D preview world.
tutorial.phantasia.scenes.s1.title: Scene Steps
tutorial.phantasia.scenes.s1.body:
Scene steps walk you through the full multi-machine layout.

Each step can show specific machines and hide others so you
focus on one part of the production chain at a time.
tutorial.phantasia.scenes.s2.title: Mistakes
tutorial.phantasia.scenes.s2.body:
Scenes can include layout validation hints called Mistakes.

Each mistake has a severity (Info / Warning / Error) and appears
in the guide view for the scene, helping players avoid common
assembly errors before they make them.
tutorial.phantasia.dev_guides.title: Creating Guides
tutorial.phantasia.dev_guides.desc: How to write and publish your own guides.
tutorial.phantasia.dev_guides.s0.title: Opening the Guide Editor
tutorial.phantasia.dev_guides.s0.body:
Go to /phantasia, open the Guides tab, and click the '+ New Guide' card.

The editor opens with a blank guide ready to fill in.
Give it a unique ID (e.g. yourmod:my_guide), a title, and an icon.
tutorial.phantasia.dev_guides.s1.title: The Guide Editor
tutorial.phantasia.dev_guides.s1.body:
The left panel is your writing area.

Type a Headline (shown large at the top of the page) and
Body Text below it. Pages are listed in the right panel.
Click '+ Add Page' to add more pages.
tutorial.phantasia.dev_guides.s2.title: Managing Pages
tutorial.phantasia.dev_guides.s2.body:
Click a page in the right panel list to select and edit it.
Click '+ Add Page' to create a new blank page.

Use Ctrl+S or the Save button to write the guide to disk.
It immediately appears in /phantasia.
tutorial.phantasia.dev_guides.s3.title: Preview and Save
tutorial.phantasia.dev_guides.s3.body:
Click 'Preview' to open the guide reader and see exactly
what players will see, including cross-links and item cards.

Click 'Save' to write to disk immediately.
The guide reloads without a restart.
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scripts.title: Writing Scripts
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scripts.desc: How to create step-by-step machine walkthroughs.
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scripts.s0.title: Opening the Script Editor
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scripts.s0.body:
Go to /phantasia, find your machine card in the Multiblocks tab,
and click it to open the scene viewer.

In the top-right of the viewer you'll find the script editor
button. A blank script is created automatically if none exists.
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scripts.s1.title: Select Mode
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scripts.s1.body:
Select is the default mode: click any block in the 3D viewport to open the Block Inspector.

The inspector shows the block's ID, blockstate properties, (and if gt is present) coil specs, lamp info, or
machine part roles.
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scripts.s2.title: Annotate Mode
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scripts.s2.body:
Switch to Annotate to place floating text labels inside
the 3D viewport. Click any position in the viewport to drop a label there.
Labels belong to the current step, they only appear while
that step is active.

Useful for calling out 'EV Energy Hatch here' or warning
players about order-sensitive assembly steps.
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scripts.s3.title: Preview Mode
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scripts.s3.body:
Click Preview to see your script exactly as a player would.

Preview plays through each step automatically: applying
camera positions, show modes, and captions in real time.
The 3D view animates just like the live guide.

Use Preview to check pacing: if a step feels too fast or
too slow, go back and adjust its tick count.
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scripts.s4.title: Steps, Ticks, and Captions
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scripts.s4.body:
Each script is a list of Steps. Use the + / - / Dup buttons
in the step row to add, remove, or duplicate steps.

The Tick field sets how long the step lasts. The Caption
field is the text shown to the player for that step.
Use the arrows to reorder steps.
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scripts.s5.title: Show Modes
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scripts.s5.body:
Row 2 of the step row controls what's visible during the step.

All: entire structure visible.
Layer: only the selected Y-layer visible.
Range: visible from layer A to layer B.
Parts, per-part toggle (useful for complex sub-assemblies).

Use Layer mode one step per layer to walk players through
building the machine from the ground up.
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scripts.s6.title: Camera Overrides
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scripts.s6.body:
Click Camera in the top bar to open the camera panel.

Each step can store its own camera angle: yaw, pitch,
zoom, and lerp type. Click 'Capture Cam' to snapshot
the current 3D viewport angle into this step.

SPRING lerp eases smoothly between steps. Set 'over N ticks'
to control how long the camera takes to travel, 20-30 is good.
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scripts.s7.title: World Items
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scripts.s7.body:
Switch to World mode (top-left of editor) to place floating
item markers directly inside the 3D viewport (currently only supports ars nouveau).

These markers are visible only during the step you place them
on, and show the player exactly what block or item goes where.

Click a position in the viewport, then pick an item from the
item picker that opens. Markers move with the camera.
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scripts.s8.title: Save and Test
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scripts.s8.body:
Click 'Save' (top-right) to write your script to disk.

Then press %s while looking at the real machine in the world
to run the script live.

Iterate fast: save, test in world, tweak, repeat.
Ctrl+S works too. If a step feels rushed, increase its tick count.
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scenes.title: Writing Scenes
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scenes.desc: How to create multi-machine Scene files.
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scenes.s0.title: What is a Scene File?
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scenes.s0.body:
A Scene groups multiple machines together in a shared 3D space.

Where a Script shows one machine at a time, a Scene can
display a whole factory floor, each machine at its real
relative offset from the others.

Find Scenes in /phantasia under the Scenes tab.
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scenes.s1.title: The Scene Editor
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scenes.s1.body:
Open the Scenes tab and click '+ New Scene': the editor opens
immediately with a blank scene ready to name and build.

The Placements panel (left) lists every machine in the scene.
Click '+ Add Machine' to add one, then set its XYZ offset
so it lines up with the others in the 3D viewport.

The viewport rotates automatically, drag to reposition.
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scenes.s2.title: Scene Steps and Visibility
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scenes.s2.body:
Like scripts, scenes have steps but each step controls which
machines are visible, not which layer of one machine.

Row 2 of the step row shows a toggle button for every machine
in the scene. Turn machines on/off per-step to guide players
through assembling a multi-machine setup in order.

Use the Caption field to tell players what to build next.
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scenes.s3.title: Camera and Save
tutorial.phantasia.dev_scenes.s3.body:
Click Camera in the top bar to open the per-step camera panel.
Works exactly like the script editor: capture yaw, pitch,
zoom, and lerp type for each step.

Click 'Save' when done. The scene appears immediately in
/phantasia under Scenes, no restart needed.

Use World mode to place item markers inside the viewport.
